rows.speaker: القائلون بهذا القول
rows.claim: A reported account says that if each arrow received exactly its allotted share, no one would bear a loss or win, so the game would not count as gambling.
rows.anchor: وقالوا : إذا كان ذلك كذلك وأخذ كل قدح نصيبه لم يبق هنالك غرم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The arrows are called aʿshār because the camel was divided into ten portions.
rows.anchor: ومن أجل ذلك قالوا لأجزاء الجزور : أعشار , لأنها عشرة أجزاء

rows.speaker: القزاز
rows.claim: Al-Qazzāz says al-tawʾam is the second gambling arrow, named for its two stakes and two camel shares; the seven winning arrows carry stakes and shares from one through seven, while three arrows carry no stake.
rows.anchor: وقال القزاز في التاء الفوقانية من ديوانه : والتوأم أحد أقداح الميسر وهو الثاني منها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The three arrows without stakes are called aghfāl, like livestock without a brand.
rows.anchor: ولذلك تدعى أغفالا لأن الغفل من الدواب الذي لا سمة له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A camel was slaughtered and apportioned into ten shares: the haunches, rump, withers, chest, back, shoulders, and thighs were divided, with neck and loose skin shared evenly.
rows.anchor: والكتفان وفيهما العضدان جزءان , والفخذان جزءان , وتقسم الرقبة والطفاطف بالسواء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The leftover bone or meat was called al-raym, a surplus beyond the load, and the butcher took it; sellers might also reserve parts, usually the extremities and head.
rows.anchor: وما بقي من عظم أو بضعة فهو الريم وأصله من الزيادة على الحمل وهي التي تسمى علاوة فيأخذ الجازر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A blindfolded handler drew the arrows from a bag while an appointed trustee shook them two or three times; blank arrows were returned to the bag.
rows.anchor: ثم يؤتى بخريطة فيها القداح واسعة الأسفل ضيقة الفم قدر ما يخرج منها سهم أو سهمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Imruʾ al-Qays compares a beloved's eyes to two arrows striking the ten shares of a slain heart: the two winning arrows capture the whole heart.
rows.anchor: قال امرؤ القيس . وما ذرفت عيناك إلا لتضربي بسهميك في أعشار قلب مقتل جعل القلب بدلا لأعشار الجزور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A blank arrow is redrawn; a winner takes the share attached to his arrow and withdraws without loss, and the drawing continues until the shares run out.
rows.anchor: فإن كان الذي خرج الفذ أخذ صاحبه جزءا وسلم من الغرم وأعاد الحرضة الإفاضة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If early winners exhaust the camel, the remaining players pay its cost; if a winner's stake exceeds the remaining shares, he takes the remainder and the others compensate the excess proportionally.
rows.anchor: فإن زادت سهام من خرج له قدح على ما بقي من الجزور غرم له من بقي ما زاد سهمه

rows.speaker: القائلون بهذا القول
rows.claim: One view divides the camel into twenty-eight portions, matching the total arrow stakes from one through seven.
rows.anchor: وقد ذكر أن الجزور تجزأ على عدد ما في القداح من الفروض وهي ثمانية وعشرون جزءا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He rejects the twenty-eight-part view here: if everyone simply took the shares attached to his arrow until all arrows were drawn, there would be no meaningful win, loss, or gambling; he initially judges the other account sounder.
rows.anchor: ولا معنى لهذا القول لأنه يلزم أن لا يكون في هذا قمار ولا فوز ولا خيبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Imruʾ al-Qays's poem, the beloved strikes the heart with al-muʿallā and al-raqīb and wins the whole heart, as a gambler can win all the camel's shares with two arrows.
rows.anchor: وما ذرفت عيناك إلا لتضربي بسهميك في أعشار قلب مقتل يقول : تضرب بسهميها المعلى والرقيب فتحوز القلب كله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An earlier gloss of Kathīr's verse says travel had emaciated the camel until it had no meat, as if two winning arrows had taken all its shares.
rows.anchor: هذه الناقة هزلها السير حتى لم يبق من لحمها شيء فكأنه ضرب عليها بالقداح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He prefers a marginal gloss: the camel's endurance makes it outpace other camels like a gambler whose arrow wins twice; this better fits the line's saying the camel itself won with two arrows.
rows.anchor: ورأيت على حاشية نسخة من كتابه ما لعله أليق

rows.speaker: كثير
rows.claim: Kathīr's verse portrays a camel passing through midday heat and night travel as though it had won with two of the arrow-drawer's arrows.
rows.anchor: ومن هذا قول كثير ووصف ناقة هزلها السير حتى أذهب لحمها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He corrects his earlier dismissal of the twenty-eight-share account: unequal stakes still produce unequal awards, since al-muʿallā yields seven of twenty-eight shares, more than arrows with six or fewer stakes.
rows.anchor: وقوله : لا معنى للتقامر عليها , على تقدير التجزئة بثمانية وعشرين ليس كذلك بل تظهر ثمرته في التفاوت في الأنصباء

rows.speaker: الأصمعي
rows.claim: Al-Aṣmaʿī is reported by the author of al-Zīna and others as supporting the twenty-eight-share division of the camel.
rows.anchor: وقد صرح صاحب الزينة وغيره عن الأصمعي كما مضى وهو ممن قال بهذا القول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Unequal results can also arise when arrows leave the bag aligned and several fall to one player; if there are fewer players than arrows, one person may win most of the camel.
rows.anchor: وربما خرج له سهمان أو ثلاثة في إفاضة واحدة لاستقامة السهام واعتدالها للخروج ففاز بمعظم الجزور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The game remains a gamble even when the number of arrows matches the players: a player may draw none and owe payment, while no one can be sure of winning.
rows.anchor: وبتقدير أن لا يخرج لكل واحد واحد يكون قمارا أيضا , لأن كل واحد منهم غير واثق بالفوز

rows.speaker: الكشاف
rows.claim: Al-Kashshāf says the participants gave their winnings to the poor and kept none for themselves; al-Biqāʿī notes this had also been transmitted from the author of al-Zīna.
rows.anchor: وقال في الكشاف : إنهم كانوا يعطون الأنصباء للفقراء ولا يأخذون منها شيئا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After condemning spending on what dims the spirit and weakens the body, the verse turns to the praiseworthy purposes on which wealth should be spent.
rows.anchor: ولما ذكر ما يذهب ضياء الروح وقوام البدن وذم النفقة فيهما اقتضى الحال السؤال عما يمدح الإنفاق فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated question about what to spend signals repeated prompting and the great importance of spending, which is among the principal supports of jihad.
rows.anchor: فأنبأ ذلك بعظم شأنها لأنها أعظم دعائم الجهاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conjunction links this spending question to the earlier question and answer about spending in 2:215, which made another spending question expectable; questions about orphans and menstruation lacked that setup.
rows.anchor: منع من توقع سؤال آخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He rejects revelation together versus separately as a sufficient reason for the conjunction, since it gives no wisdom and many revelation reports show conjunctions; the last revealed verse, 2:281, also begins with wa.
rows.anchor: وادعاء أن سبب العطف النزول جملة وسبب القطع النزول مفرقا مع كونه غير شاف للغلة بعدم بيان الحكمة

rows.speaker: البيهقي
rows.claim: The author cites al-Bayhaqī and al-Wāḥidī for reports that 2:281 was the final revealed verse, noting its opening conjunction; al-Bukhārī also gives it a chapter heading.
rows.anchor: أخرجه البيهقي في الدلائل والواحدي من وجهين في مقدمة أسباب النزول

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Ḥarālī reads the conjunction as reinforcing the repeated seeking twice, like the Israelites' case; this community may have avoided asking a third time, unlike them.
rows.anchor: وقال الحرالي : في العطف إنباء بتأكد التلدد مرتين كما في قصة بني إسرائيل

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Ḥarālī defines al-ʿafw as what a person freely gives without strain; the command encourages giving the surplus but does not make that level obligatory, preserving ease for this community.
rows.anchor: وهو ما سمحت به النفس من غير كلفة

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Ḥarālī sorts spending into obligatory alms, dispensable surplus that should not be hoarded, and contested property whose donation requires striving and becomes a trade for the afterlife.
rows.anchor: فصار المنفق على ثلاث رتب : رتبة حق مفروض لا بد منه وهي الصدقة المفروضة

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: When a woman asked what she could give from her husband's wealth, the Prophet answered fresh fruit: it may be eaten or gifted before it spoils.
rows.anchor: قالت امرأة للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم : ما يحل لنا من أموال أزواجنا - تسأل عن الإنفاق منها , قال : الرطب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here al-rutab is vocalized with ḍamma on rāʾ and sukūn on ṭāʾ; it means produce such as grapes and melons, cooked foods, or other things that spoil if kept overnight.
rows.anchor: لأنه من العفو الذي يضر إمساكه بفساده ؛ لأن الرطب هو ما إذا أبقي ين يوم إلى يوم تغير كالعنب والبطيخ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Restricting the recommended gift to freely disposable surplus cautions the drinker before wine was forbidden: intoxicated dealings are generally invalid and regretted on sobering; gambling is worse.
rows.anchor: وفي تخصيص المنفق بالعفو منع لمتعاطي الخمر قبل حرمتها من التصرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command's late clarification that spending is urged on surplus could inspire self-sacrifice among believers in hardship without imposing a burden; 2:177 had already praised giving wealth despite love of it.
rows.anchor: ولعل تأخير بيان أن المحثوث عليه من النفقة إنما هو الفضل إلى هذا المحل ليحمل أهل الدين الرغبة فيه

rows.speaker: الأصبهاني
rows.claim: Al-Aṣbahānī reports exegetes' view that people kept a year's household needs from gold, silver, crops, and livestock, or one day's needs if they worked, and donated the rest until the zakat verse abrogated this rule.
rows.anchor: قال الأصبهاني : قال أهل التفسير : كان الرجل بعد نزول هذه الآية إذا كان له ذهب أو فضة أو زرع أو ضرع ينظر ما يكفيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Having detailed the rulings and spending through varied explanations, the verse reassures that God explains the signs likewise; al-Ḥarālī says the plural covers the heart, soul, body, and a person's dealings with others.
rows.anchor: قال الحرالي : فجمعها لأنها آيات من جهات مختلفات لما يرجع لأمر القلب وللنفس وللجسم ولحال المرء مع غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The initial singular address raises the statement's rank and turns it toward the Prophet, already filled with knowledge; the plural then addresses followers according to their understanding and aspiration. Alternatively, the syntax repeats the act of explaining.
rows.anchor: وأفرد الخطاب أولا وجمع ثانيا إعلاما بعظمة هذا القول للإقبال به على الرأس

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Ḥarālī takes the phrase as preparing people for reflection, the soul's hand for grasping knowledge as the body's hand grasps sensible things.
rows.anchor: المعلومات كما تنال بيد الجسم المحسوسات - قاله الحرالي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author links this verse's divine attributes with 7:54, which says creation and command belong to God, and 30:27, which calls His likeness supreme.
rows.anchor: ولما في العلو من الظهور وفي العظمة من الخفاء لموضع الإحاطة لأن العظيم هو ما يستغرق

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet reports God's saying that pride is His cloak and majesty His wrap: the cloak is outward, while the wrap covers what is inward and below.
rows.anchor: قال سبحانه وتعالى فيما أنبأ عنه نبيه صلى الله عليه وسلم ( الكبرياء ردائي ) لأن الرداء هو ما على الظاهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's greatness is hidden in detail while His pride and loftiness appear most clearly in what is general; the sky manifests His pride, earth His majesty, the Throne His height, and the Kursī His greatness.
rows.anchor: فإذا في السماء كبرياؤه وفي الأرض عظمته , وفي العرش علوه وفي الكرسي عظمته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse's rank follows from its disclosure of God's sustaining power, loftiness, and greatness, and from its establishing Islam's religion of surrender; this follows the earlier affirmation of the upright religion and Āl ʿImrān 3:18.
rows.anchor: فتبين بهذا المعنى علو رتبة هذه الآية بما علت على الإيمان علو الإيمان على الكفران

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A good reading of the path imagery links it to 6:153: plural darknesses reflect the many errors of sealed senses, while the singular light is the one truth that repairs the heart and brings benefit.
rows.anchor: ومن المحامل الحسنة أن يشار بالجمع إلى ما ينشأ من الجهل عن المشاعر التي أخبر بالختم عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Disbelievers cover rational and transmitted proofs with their desires; their patrons include those desires and whatever leads them into transgression, such as devils and idol worship.
rows.anchor: أي ستروا ما دلت عليه أدلة العقول أولا والنقول ثانيا بشهوات النفوس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural pronoun and darknesses suit the many kinds of disbelief; the light is the innate, primordial light from which the disbelievers are taken.
rows.anchor: وإسناده إلى ضمير الجمع يؤيد أن جمع الظلمات لكثرة أنواع الكفر

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Ḥarālī says all creatures share the reality of the first light, the first spirit, and the upright primordial nature, as in the report that every newborn is born upon the fitra.
rows.anchor: قال الحرالي : وفيه بيان استواء جميع الخلق في حقيقة النور الأول إلى الروح المجندة إلى الفطرة المستوية

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Ḥarālī explains that they are called companions of the Fire because they followed it without realizing it, since a companion is one who follows his companion.
rows.anchor: قال الحرالي : الذين اتبعوها من حيث لم يشعروا من حيث إن الصاحب من اتبع مصحوبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The emphatic they marks the disbelievers' exclusive attachment to the Fire, and their being described as abiding forever suggests that they were already in it during worldly life, according to al-Ḥarālī.
rows.anchor: قال الحرالي : وجعل الخلود وصفا لهم إشعارا بأنهم فيها وهم في دنياهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After God's majesty, the believers' allegiance, and the disbelievers' rejection, the Abraham and ruined-town narratives demonstrate divine power and recall the people revived after death in 2:243; al-Ḥarālī says this elevated point is addressed specifically to the Prophet.
rows.anchor: أخذ يدل على ذلك بقصة المحاج للخليل والمار على القرية مذكرا بقصة الذين قال لهم موتوا ثم أحياهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question means know as though witnessing directly, owing to the Prophet's complete insight and the illuminating meanings God placed within him.
rows.anchor: أي تعلم بما نخبرك به علما هو عندك كالمشاهدة لما لك من كمال البصيرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opponent is Nimrod; Abraham is the Arabs' forefather, whom they especially ought to follow. The pronoun in his Lord can refer to Abraham or his disputant, and the dispute concerns the creator and benefactor despite clear proofs and innate guidance.
rows.anchor: الضمير يصح أن يعود على كل منهما أي فيما يختص به خالقه المربي له المحسن إليه

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Ḥarālī says worldly kingship is a trial for its recipient; Nimrod's sovereignty fed pride instead of gratitude and led him to imagine he deserved the kingship of the Lord of all dominion.
rows.anchor: قال الحرالي : وفي إشعاره أن الملك فتنة وبلاء على من أوتيه

words: إِذْ قَالَ إِبْرَٰهِۦمُ رَبِّىَ ٱلَّذِى يُحْىِۦ وَيُمِيتُ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The story of those told to die and then revived in 2:243 proves resurrection on a Day without sale, friendship, or intercession and prepares for Abraham's argument.
rows.anchor: دلالة على البعث ليوم لا بيع فيه ولا خلة ولا شفاعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham says his Lord alone gives life and death; the wording implies an earlier exchange and someone claiming to share this divine attribute.
rows.anchor: وهذه العبارة تدل على تقدم كلام في هذا وادعاء أحد لمشاركة في هذه الصفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nimrod boasts that he gives life and death by pardoning someone liable to execution and killing someone who did not deserve death; this is a bold, unreflective misuse of his power over others.
rows.anchor: بأن أمن على من استحق القتل وأقتل من لا يستحق القتل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeing that the life-and-death claim might become obscure or prolonged, Abraham shifts to an unmistakable challenge that will silence Nimrod and expose his weakness.
rows.anchor: فلما رأى إبراهيم عليه الصلاة والسلام أنه قد اجترأ على عظيم وأن محاجته في نفس الإحياء ربما خفيت أو طالت

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Ḥarālī says sound disputation avoids wrangling over a confusing proof and shifts to an outwardly clear argument, citing 18:53 as printed in the source.
rows.anchor: وقال الحرالي : ولما كان من حسن الاحتجاج ترك المراء بمتابعة الحجة الملبسة كما قال تعالى

words: فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَأْتِى بِٱلشَّمْسِ مِنَ ٱلْمَشْرِقِ
rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Ḥarālī describes a shift from proof within the self to proof in the cosmos, using the sun, and links the two kinds of signs to 41:53.
rows.anchor: نقل المحاج من الحجة الواقعة في الأنفس إلى الحجة الواقعة في الآفاق بأعظم كواكبها الشمس

words: فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَأْتِى بِٱلشَّمْسِ مِنَ ٱلْمَشْرِقِ
rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Ḥarālī says the apparent move from human life to the sun still completes the first proof: the soul is the body's sun, and giving life is like bringing that sun up from where it set.
rows.anchor: ففي ظاهر الاحتجاج انتقال وفي طيه تقرير الأول لأن الروح شمس البدن

words: فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَأْتِى بِٱلشَّمْسِ مِنَ ٱلْمَشْرِقِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God created the sun and brings it from the east each day, ages before Nimrod existed; Abraham challenges him to bring it from the west even once.
rows.anchor: أي تسبب عن دعواك هذه أو أقول لك : إن { الله } بما له من العظمة والجلال

words: فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَأْتِى بِٱلشَّمْسِ مِنَ ٱلْمَشْرِقِ
rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Ḥarālī says the challenge shows that one Lord governs both human life and death and the sun's rising and setting; the sun's eventual rising in the west anticipates the Hour and the return of souls from bodies.
rows.anchor: وفي لحنه إشعار بأن الله سبحانه وتعالى لا بد وأن يأتي بالشمس من المغرب ليكون في ذلك إظهار تصريفه لها

rows.speaker: الحرالي
rows.claim: Al-Ḥarālī derives bahita from bewilderment that leaves someone frozen in the same state and form under the impact of something overwhelming.
rows.anchor: قال الحرالي : من البهت وهو بقاء الشيء على حاله وصورته لا يتغير عنها لأمر يبهره وقعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nimrod is confounded because the challenge proves he cannot change even a form God made, much less create from nothing or breathe life into it; Abraham exposes his denial of God's exclusive power.
rows.anchor: فكيف له بأن يوجد صورة من العدم فكيف ثم كيف بإفاضة الروح عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nimrod wronged by claiming divine power and by executing the innocent while sparing the guilty; God's refusal to guide the unjust generalizes to those who put things out of place and whose hearts become dark.
rows.anchor: لأنه ظلم في ادعائه ذلك وفي الوجه الذي ادعى ذلك بسبه من قتل البريء وترك المجترئ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shortened negative statement about guidance conveys generality; al-Imām says the concise wording yields greater meaning, a Qur'anic subtlety.
rows.anchor: وقصر فعل الهداية لإفادة العموم , قال الإمام : فاختصر اللفظ إفادة لزيادة المعنى وهو من اللطائف القرآنية
